scope: Specified exp24 code and formal-v2/preflight/identity-v1 evidence only; formal-v1 excluded; no manuscript/graphics review or native Store rerun.

findings.finding: Cross-process loopback reads establish byte correctness, but do not establish that payload bytes traversed TCP rather than a local-copy optimization.
evidence: formal-v2/client-B.log:10-15 reports protocol tcp, TcpTransport listening, MC_STORE_MEMCPY not set ... memcpy enabled, and global segment size 0.

freeze.py:26-35 and records op-001/op-002 confirm A owns 128 MiB and B has global_size=0; all 40 primary reads are B. These controls remove the same-client case but do not identify the executed transfer branch.
worker.py:18 selects tcp; the permitted evidence contains no per-transfer branch trace or payload socket-byte accounting. summary.json scope nevertheless labels the run single-host TCP.
findings.suggestedfix: Describe these as TCP-configured cross-process local Store calls with the payload path unverified. Before claiming measured TCP payload transport, record the effective local-copy setting and branch/socket evidence tied to the known-object reads; use a separate controlled run if needed. Do not combine v1 and v2.

findings.finding: Audit acceptance does not enforce client/stage/request correlation, and the summary reports read-client identities from the plan.
evidence: audit.py:6-8 validates id/op, but not client/stage/key or request arguments. worker.py:23-30 does not echo key/request digest/PID; runner.py:75 supplies client/stage from the planned case.

In-memory mutation of op-007 client B to A, or stage normal to master-down, still yields pass and accepted=true. After the client mutation, summarize.py:31 still emits primary_data_get_clients=[B]. Altering that planned get key also leaves audit accepted.
The actual 238 rows independently match planned id/op/client/stage and call order; no such mismatch was found in formal-v2. Current hashes for all four frozen source files match plan.code_sha256.
findings.suggestedfix: Compare client and stage during audit, derive client summaries from validated observations, and have the worker echo a request digest/key and process identity. Bind the record stream to its run/plan/code hashes so the claimed execution context can be checked with the rows.

findings.finding: A failed audit still lets runner.py return normally, so freeze.py subprocess check=True is not an acceptance gate.
evidence: runner.py:87-92 writes and prints the audit but never raises when accepted=false; freeze.py:81 checks only subprocess exit status.

A bounded in-memory invocation of the actual runner with a synthetic IPC timeout produced planned=1, fail=1, accepted=false, then returned normally. No native Store, real worker process, or filesystem output was used.
Actual formal-v2 audit is accepted with zero fail/missing; this is a recorder failure-path defect, not an observed failed formal run.
findings.suggestedfix: After preserving raw rows, audit and cleanup evidence, return nonzero when audit acceptance fails. Keep observed outcomes separate from assertion passes and retain every planned operation in the denominator.

findings.finding: The summarizer does not apply the auditor finite/nonnegative latency filter.
evidence: audit.py:44-48 excludes missing, nonfinite, boolean and negative latency samples; summarize.py:19-25 includes every assertion-pass latency.
In-memory op-007 latency=-1 leaves audit.valid_latency_samples=119 while the summary claims 120 valid timings and emits min_ms=-1. Setting it to null raises TypeError.
All 238 actual latencies are finite and nonnegative; all 120 actual timing samples and all 12 distributions independently reproduce exactly.
findings.suggestedfix: Use one latency-eligibility predicate in audit and summarize. Report invalid timing separately from operation outcome, retaining planned/failed/missing/observed denominators.

byte_checks.basis: SHA-256 of worker-returned bytes compared with independent SHAKE-256 seed/size reconstruction; raw payload bytes are not retained in these artifacts.

plan_code.coverage: freeze.py, runner.py, worker.py, audit.py; summarize.py is outside the formal code-hash map. Archived code and environment/lifecycle files were outside the allowlist and were not inspected.

timings.clock_scope: Worker-local perf_counter_ns difference around Python Store dispatch/call. Excludes put payload generation, returned-byte hashing, JSON/IPC and parent overhead; includes Python/native API overhead. Descriptive serial local measurements, not network-only latency or a load benchmark.

verified.duplicate_put: op-126/128/130/132 all return 0. Each following B get returns 4096 bytes with original hash f3a232da7410798742cad8b30b408d34bf75e7479adbddff0c734dca58f35b82, including changed-content and changed-size writes. Return 0 does not demonstrate overwrite.
verified.empty_get: op-003 (absent key) and op-218 (master down) both return b-empty with the empty SHA-256. B log:16-17 ties the latter to RPC_FAIL; accompanying master-down is_exist/put return -900. Audit ambiguous=0 describes the planned byte-shape assertions, not semantic disambiguation of miss versus error. No zero-length put case was tested.
verified.restart: Runner explicitly disables HA, snapshots, snapshot restore and offload. Existing and fresh clients report survivor is_exist=0 and empty get after restart; fresh C can put/get/hash/remove a new object. This is bounded non-HA metadata/recovery behavior, not a test of HA or physical byte erasure. The first probe follows a planned 3-second sleep; after12s means 12 more seconds after that probe, not 12 seconds since restart. Per-call absolute start timestamps are absent.
verified.cleanup: 40 normal remove/absence pairs, duplicate remove/absence, C recovery remove/absence, and survivor/down-write absence readbacks match. The last two removes return -704 after restart, then is_exist=0. A/B/C close return 0. cleanup.json records five owned PIDs exited, all five named ports closed, and plan unchanged; this is recorded cleanup evidence, not a new live Linux process/port inspection or proof of clearing every physical buffer/dynamic listener.
verified.binary_identity: Preflight package/version/wheel hash matches the formal plan and all six reported installed/native-file hashes match wheel entries. Native files were not independently reread here; binary_build_commit_verified=false prevents attributing this wheel to source_read_commit.
verified.identity_v1: 12/12 cases, all recorded keys, current identity.py hash and four gate controls reproduce; exactly one case is eligible with both literal boolean flags. This is exact full-prefix caller metadata equality. The key hashes metadata, not payload; flags are caller attestations, not byte verification/importer execution. Tenant metadata supplies no authentication/Store ACL, and opaque revision labels require caller completeness. These limits are explicit in identity.py; no model/tokenizer/KV reuse was exercised.

bounded_checks.method: Standard-library reconciliation and in-memory mutation/stub execution of the inspected modules; source/evidence left unchanged.
bounded_checks.positive_controls: Wrong op/hash/incomplete replies fail; a missing row stays in planned=238 and makes acceptance false.
